about: Spec 3.9.0 (acp.md *The model last used in a directory*; *Scheduled work*, *The run's model*). Three kinds. `kind: start` — the device: which model a session of its own starts on. `asked`: the model asked for at the start (--model; model / lembas_model in session/new); `project`: `model` in a trusted project's configuration; `directory`: the model remembered for exactly this directory; `global`: `model` in the device's global configuration; `served`: the ids the login serves now; `default`: the instance's default. → `{model, from}`, `from` one of `asked`, `project`, `directory`, `global`, `default`. Only the directory's model is checked against `served` and skipped when it is not there; the others are taken as written (a model nobody serves is that source's own error, as before). `kind: record` — the device: whether something makes the session's model the directory's. `session`: `terminal`, `link` (a session the client opened, or a terminal's shared one), `stdio`, `run` (one-shot lembas run) or `scheduled` (a session a schedule opened for its run); `agent`: `main` or `subagent`; `what`: `turn` (a turn begins; `machine: true` when the harness started it), `change` (the person changes the session's model: /model, a setting, _lembas/configure) or `command` (a command's own model, for its prompt). → true or false. `kind: client` — the client (LLeMbas): the model a new agent chat on a device and directory, or a schedule's run there, starts on. `named`: the model the person chose for the chat, or the schedule names (absent: none); `directory`: `model` of the directory in the device's _lembas/directories answer (absent: none, an older device, or a device not asked); `has`: the models the person has now; `default`: what a chat or schedule without a model started on before 3.9.0. → `{model, from}`, `from` one of `named`, `directory`, `default`. CLI: src/session/lastmodel.ts.

cases.about: Nothing but the instance's default.
The global setting — what a login writes — over the instance's default.
The model last used in this directory over the global setting.
The project's setting over the directory's memory: it is written down on purpose.
The model asked for over everything.
The remembered model is no longer served: skipped, the global setting decides.
…and with no global setting, the instance's default.
A global setting is not checked against the list here: it is taken as written.
A person's turn in a terminal.
A person's turn in a session the client opened.
An editor's session.
The person switches model.
The chat's model is changed from the client between turns.
A turn the harness started — a finished job's note — is nobody's choice.
A subagent's model is not the directory's.
A command's own model holds for its prompt only.
A one-shot run from a script.
A scheduled run never becomes the directory's model.
…nor does a model change on a schedule's session.
A new agent chat, no model chosen, the directory remembers one the person has.
The person chose a model: theirs, whatever the directory remembers.
The person no longer has the remembered model: as before.
An older device, or one that remembers nothing there: as before.
An Agentic schedule that names no model follows the directory.
A schedule that names one runs on it.
The directory's model is compared exactly: another spelling is not the model.
